hook: Demis Hassabis showed an early talent for chess, reaching master strength as a teenager, before studying computer science at Cambridge and going on to design the video game Theme Park and lead AI programming on Black and White at Lionhead Studios. After running his own studio, Elixir Studios, he returned to academia and earned a PhD in cognitive neuroscience from University College London in 2009, studying memory and imagination. In 2010 he co-founded DeepMind with Shane Legg and Mustafa Suleyman to pursue general purpose learning systems, and Google acquired the company in 2014. Under his leadership DeepMind built landmark reinforcement learning systems, including AlphaGo, which defeated Go world champion Lee Sedol in 2016, and AlphaFold, which predicts the three dimensional structure of proteins from their amino acid sequences. Following a 2023 merger with Google Brain, he now leads the combined organization as co-founder and CEO of Google DeepMind. In 2024 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, shared with John Jumper and David Baker, for work on protein structure prediction, and was knighted for services to artificial intelligence.
